entries.text: The chat agent can now read library docs.

Libraries can now ship their own docs in a `docs/` folder next to their manifest. See
[Writing Docs for Your Library](https://docs.griptapenodes.com/en/stable/development/custom_nodes/library_documentation/).

Scanning workflows (project switch, engine start, registry refresh) now sends at most ten
`EngineInitializationProgress` events a second instead of two per workflow. Failures and the
final event are still sent, so clients that counted every per-workflow event receive fewer.

Load 3D's Save Snapshot fills the node's `image` output again: a serialized artifact dict
keeps its `metadata` when it's normalized into an artifact.
[#6311](https://github.com/griptape-ai/griptape-nodes-engine/issues/6311)

`Workflow Node`s that run at the same time, in parallel branches or in a loop set to
"Run Group Items All at Once", now each load their workflow into a flow of their own. Before,
one node could silently load the same copy of the workflow as another node, or load its copy
into the wrong flow, so the run could use another node's workflow without any error.
[#5665](https://github.com/griptape-ai/griptape-nodes-engine/issues/5665)

Deleting a node while its workflow is running, or deleting two nodes at the same time, no longer
lets other requests see the node being deleted as the current node, or mix up which node each
delete is working on.
[#5665](https://github.com/griptape-ai/griptape-nodes-engine/issues/5665)

The editor can again switch projects, open workflows, and create workflows. Requests that name no
workflow act on the only open workflow again, instead of failing with "the request names no
workflow".

End Flow's `result_details` now shows only the current run's `[SUCCEEDED]` or `[FAILED]` status.
Before, it added another status line on every run when nothing was connected to it, and saving
kept the extra lines in the workflow.
[#6304](https://github.com/griptape-ai/griptape-nodes-engine/issues/6304)

Running a node again while another node is still running no longer fails with only the node's
name as the error. Before, the node also refused every later run until the other node finished,
and then ran by itself anyway.
[#5562](https://github.com/griptape-ai/griptape-nodes-engine/issues/5562)

`AppInitializationComplete` now includes `engine_run_id`, so a client can tell when the engine
restarted without waiting for a heartbeat.
[#6213](https://github.com/griptape-ai/griptape-nodes-engine/issues/6213)

`CloseWorkflowRequest`, also an MCP tool, closes an open workflow.
[#6205](https://github.com/griptape-ai/griptape-nodes-engine/issues/6205)

`DescribeNodeTypeRequest` takes `include_metadata`, `include_tooltips`, and `include_ui_options`,
so callers can leave those parts out of the response.
[#5919](https://github.com/griptape-ai/griptape-nodes-engine/issues/5919)

`ListOpenWorkflowsRequest`, also an MCP tool, lists the open workflows.
[#6221](https://github.com/griptape-ai/griptape-nodes-engine/issues/6221)

ForEach Group and ForLoop Group have a "Flatten Results" setting that merges the lists each
iteration returns into one flat `results` list. "Flatten Depth" limits how many levels it
flattens.
[#6315](https://github.com/griptape-ai/griptape-nodes-engine/issues/6315)

The engine can keep several workflows open at once, one per editor tab. Opening a workflow no
longer closes the one already open.
See [Transports](https://github.com/griptape-ai/griptape-nodes-engine/blob/HEAD/docs/guides/transports.md#open-workflows).
[#6231](https://github.com/griptape-ai/griptape-nodes-engine/issues/6231)

Open workflows reported to clients, such as in the heartbeat's `open_workflows`, now include
`display_name` and `is_saved`.
[#6221](https://github.com/griptape-ai/griptape-nodes-engine/issues/6221)

`OpenWorkflowRequest`, also an MCP tool, opens a saved workflow or a new unsaved one alongside
any already open.
[#6221](https://github.com/griptape-ai/griptape-nodes-engine/issues/6221)
[#6241](https://github.com/griptape-ai/griptape-nodes-engine/issues/6241)

Results of requests that open, load, or save a workflow now include `open_workflow`, the workflow
open after the request.
[#6199](https://github.com/griptape-ai/griptape-nodes-engine/issues/6199)

`SaveWorkflowRequest` takes `continue_in_copy`, which keeps you working in the new file after a
Save As or versioned save. See [Transports](https://github.com/griptape-ai/griptape-nodes-engine/blob/HEAD/docs/guides/transports.md#open-workflows).
[#6228](https://github.com/griptape-ai/griptape-nodes-engine/issues/6228)

Requests about a saved workflow, such as `RenameWorkflowRequest` and `DeleteWorkflowRequest`, now
take a `workflow_id`, which stays the same when the workflow is renamed or moved. See
[Transports](https://github.com/griptape-ai/griptape-nodes-engine/blob/HEAD/docs/guides/transports.md#open-workflows) for the full list.
[#6227](https://github.com/griptape-ai/griptape-nodes-engine/issues/6227)

Clients now receive `WorkflowOpenedEvent` and `WorkflowClosedEvent` when a workflow opens or
closes. See [Transports](https://github.com/griptape-ai/griptape-nodes-engine/blob/HEAD/docs/guides/transports.md#getting-results-back).
[#6213](https://github.com/griptape-ai/griptape-nodes-engine/issues/6213)

`WorkflowNotOpenResultFailure` now lists the open workflows in `open_workflows`.
[#6234](https://github.com/griptape-ai/griptape-nodes-engine/issues/6234)

**Breaking:** `ExecutionEvent` and `ProgressEvent` now name their workflow in `open_workflow_id`
instead of `workflow_id`, matching results.
See [MIGRATION.md](https://github.com/griptape-ai/griptape-nodes-engine/blob/HEAD/MIGRATION.md#execution-events-name-their-workflow-in-open_workflow_id).
[#6240](https://github.com/griptape-ai/griptape-nodes-engine/issues/6240)

**Breaking:** `EngineHeartbeatResultSuccess.current_workflow_id` is removed. Read
`open_workflows` instead.
[#6261](https://github.com/griptape-ai/griptape-nodes-engine/issues/6261)

Starting the engine, switching projects, and refreshing the workflow registry are faster on
projects with many workflows. Scanning 500 workflows takes about 280 ms instead of 770 ms.

Opening a Griptape-provided workflow now opens an unsaved copy.
[#6229](https://github.com/griptape-ai/griptape-nodes-engine/issues/6229)

An MCP session without an `X-Griptape-Workflow-Id` header now stays on the workflow it last used,
instead of moving to another open workflow when that one closes.
[#6234](https://github.com/griptape-ai/griptape-nodes-engine/issues/6234)

`RunWorkflowFromScratchRequest` and `RunWorkflowFromRegistryRequest` now ignore the envelope's
`open_workflow_id`, so they no longer fail when it names a closed workflow.
[#6198](https://github.com/griptape-ai/griptape-nodes-engine/issues/6198)

`RequestClient` now receives results on its own topic instead of the `response` topic every
connected editor receives.
[#6240](https://github.com/griptape-ai/griptape-nodes-engine/issues/6240)

A result's `open_workflow_id` is now `null` for requests about the engine rather than one
workflow, such as `ClearAllObjectStateRequest`, instead of echoing the id the request was sent
with. See [Transports](https://github.com/griptape-ai/griptape-nodes-engine/blob/HEAD/docs/guides/transports.md#getting-results-back).
[#6213](https://github.com/griptape-ai/griptape-nodes-engine/issues/6213)

Requests that name no workflow, sent from an MCP session without one or directly to an `Engine`,
now act on none. Requests that need a workflow fail with `WorkflowNotNamedResultFailure` instead
of answering as if it were empty. Node library code that reads the current workflow from a thread
it started itself now finds none. Start the thread with `asyncio.to_thread` to keep the node's
workflow.
[#6235](https://github.com/griptape-ai/griptape-nodes-engine/issues/6235)

`SetWorkflowContextRequest` and `EnsureWorkflowAndFlowRequest` now fail for an unknown `unsaved:`
name instead of creating a workflow for it.
[#6221](https://github.com/griptape-ai/griptape-nodes-engine/issues/6221)

**Breaking:** The MCP server and chat agent no longer offer `ExecuteNodeRequest` as a tool. Use
`ResolveNodeRequest` to run a single node.

A closed unsaved workflow no longer stays in the workflow list or reopens as an empty canvas.
[#6232](https://github.com/griptape-ai/griptape-nodes-engine/issues/6232)

`SetWorkflowContextRequest` and `EnsureWorkflowAndFlowRequest` no longer open a saved workflow
without its nodes, which made the next save erase the file.
[#6221](https://github.com/griptape-ai/griptape-nodes-engine/issues/6221)

Deleting the current flow by name no longer leaves the engine sending requests to the deleted
flow until it restarts.
[#6305](https://github.com/griptape-ai/griptape-nodes-engine/issues/6305)

Directory parameters set to an absolute, `~`, or `file://` path containing `{###}`, such as
`/renders/shot_v{###}`, now create the next free version folder instead of failing with
"missing required variables: _index".
[griptape-nodes-library-standard#945](https://github.com/griptape-ai/griptape-nodes-library-standard/issues/945)

A workflow file that fails to load no longer stays open half built, blocking the next workflow
from opening.
[#6260](https://github.com/griptape-ai/griptape-nodes-engine/issues/6260)

Renaming a workflow that isn't open no longer saves the open workflow under the new name and
deletes the renamed workflow's file.
[#6227](https://github.com/griptape-ai/griptape-nodes-engine/issues/6227)

When the app reopens a session on an engine that is now offline, such as one on another machine, it no longer says "Can't reach your engine" about the engine on this computer. It says it can't reach the engine you last used and offers **Use this computer's engine**.

With a custom Griptape server endpoint, the engine no longer keeps trying to reach a relay the server doesn't serve. Turn on **Route relay traffic through this server** in Settings once your administrator has enabled the relay on the admin server, or set `GTN_DESKTOP_ROUTE_RELAY_THROUGH_SERVER`.

Node libraries can read the destination a connected `File Output Settings` node supplies with
`GetConnectedFileDestinationRequest`, which works in a worker, and rebuild it with
`file_destination_from_spec`. `GetConnectedDirectoryDestinationRequest` and
`GetConnectedFileSequenceDestinationRequest` do the same for directory and file sequence outputs.
[#5971](https://github.com/griptape-ai/griptape-nodes-engine/issues/5971)

`local_objects.drop` and `local_objects.drop_all` now free a library's object as soon as they
are called, even while nodes are running, instead of waiting until no node is running. A library
switching models now frees the old model before loading the new one, rather than holding both
in GPU memory until the run ends.

Directory parameters built with `ProjectDirectoryParameter` now use an absolute, `~/...`, or
`file://` path as the destination instead of nesting it inside the outputs directory. A plain
name still goes through the situation template and is versioned. Web addresses are rejected with
an error.
[#6237](https://github.com/griptape-ai/griptape-nodes-engine/issues/6237)

Nodes running in a worker or inside an Isolated Execution group now save with the name, location
and "If File Exists" policy from a connected `File Output Settings` node, instead of their own
defaults.
[#5971](https://github.com/griptape-ai/griptape-nodes-engine/issues/5971)

A saved workflow run without `--project-file-path` now fails when its configured project (the
`project_file` setting, else the workspace's `griptape-nodes-project.yml`) cannot be activated,
instead of running on system defaults.
[#6214](https://github.com/griptape-ai/griptape-nodes-engine/issues/6214)

Running a saved workflow from the command line no longer writes `storage_backend` to your config
file, so it no longer switches the editor's storage backend. `--storage-backend` now applies to
the run it is passed to instead of the next one, and leaving it out uses the configured backend
instead of `local`.

A loop body copy of a node now keeps every value the canvas node holds, including inputs fed by
connections, so a node whose parameters depend on an input (such as a diffusers node whose
`image_references` depends on `pipeline`) no longer loses them when the loop runs. The copy's
connections are made the way a saved workflow makes them, so they push nothing into nodes while the
body is still being assembled, and a saved value the copy refuses on a connected input is logged and
skipped instead of stopping the loop.
[#6104](https://github.com/griptape-ai/griptape-nodes-engine/issues/6104)

`ForEach Group`, `For Loop Group` and other loop groups show one way in and one way out, `Start Loop`
and `On Complete`. The second `Flow In` / `Flow Out` pair, which nothing read at run time, is gone, so a
chain wired through `Flow Out` no longer stops silently at the loop. Workflows saved with connections on
`Flow In` or `Flow Out` load unchanged and the connections move to `Start Loop` and `On Complete`.
[#6250](https://github.com/griptape-ai/griptape-nodes-engine/issues/6250)

A loop with nodes in its body no longer collects an empty list when the start node's
`current_item` or `index` is wired straight into the end node's `new_item_to_add`. A ForEach or
For Loop group whose own `current_item` or `index` is wired into its own `new_item_to_add` now
runs and collects the items instead of being skipped by the run.
[#6238](https://github.com/griptape-ai/griptape-nodes-engine/issues/6238)

`make run` and `make run/refresh` no longer fail with "The syntax of the command is incorrect"
on Windows when make runs recipes through `cmd.exe`.
[#6174](https://github.com/griptape-ai/griptape-nodes-engine/issues/6174)

A node now saves where a `File Output Settings` node wired to it says when the wire crosses a
group boundary: the node inside the group and the settings node outside it, the other way round,
or each in its own group. Before, it saved with its own default name, location and
existing-file policy.
[#6146](https://github.com/griptape-ai/griptape-nodes-engine/issues/6146)

A loop run locally with `run_in_order` off no longer collects the item of a pass that exited
through `skip_iteration`, so filter loops return the filtered list in parallel too. Loops in an
isolated or published execution environment still collect skipped passes.
[#6247](https://github.com/griptape-ai/griptape-nodes-engine/issues/6247)

Agents can fill `ParameterList` inputs such as `items` on Create Image List. A single-item
connection aimed at the list itself now fails with a message saying to add a slot with
`AddParameterToNodeRequest(parent_container_name=...)` and connect to the slot it returns. The
request's tool description and the `griptape-nodes-workflows` skill teach the same steps.
[#5147](https://github.com/griptape-ai/griptape-nodes-engine/issues/5147)

A process running the engine no longer risks crashing with a segmentation fault as it exits after
refreshing a preview or syncing workflows. The threads that watch those files now stop before
Python shuts down.

Engines that use a Griptape license (`GRIPTAPE_NODES_LICENSE`) can now be reached through the
Griptape Cloud relay. The license takes precedence over `GT_CLOUD_API_KEY`.

An engine can now run a library's nodes on another engine named in
`distributed_execution.library_engines`, reaching it directly when that engine sets
`transports.websocket_direct.advertise_url` and through Griptape Cloud otherwise. An engine that
sets `advertise_url` now reports itself to the engine registry even without Griptape Cloud.

A request envelope's `open_workflow_id` now reaches the engine and comes back on the result,
including on the app's own failures for denied or unreadable requests. Progress events the app
forwards name their node's workflow in `workflow_id`.

Griptape Nodes Engine is pinned to 0.108.0. See its
[release notes](https://github.com/griptape-ai/griptape-nodes-engine/releases/tag/v0.108.0).
The editor installed with the `editor` extra is pinned to 0.130.0.

With the "Rich text inputs" beta feature on (Settings → "Beta Features"), a text field can reference
the parameters of other nodes in the same flow, except nodes inside ForEach, ForLoop and While
groups. Typing `{` and part of a node's name lists the nodes, and typing `.` after one lists its
parameters that have an output, so `{node.parameter}` can be picked instead of typed. Picking a
parameter that has no variable yet, or hovering one, offers "Add variable and connect node" and
shows the parameter's current value. Enter confirms it, and the prompt closes at once while a
placeholder node shows where the new node will go. It creates a variable of that name from that
value and adds a "Create Variable: node.parameter" node to the right of the parameter, connected
to it. The variable holds the value from the last time the whole flow ran, so a change to the
source shows up on the next run.

**Settings → Node Settings → Dot Size** scales Dot nodes and their ports on the canvas, from half
to three times the default size.

The "Connect" tab of the engine picker has an "Organization" dropdown when you belong to more than
one organization. It lists that organization's engines, and "Generate API Key" creates keys in it.

"Add to Griptape Nodes" links can pin a library to a branch, tag, or commit with a `ref`
parameter, for example `#library-management?git=<repo>&ref=stable`. The ref fills in **Branch /
Tag / Commit** under **Advanced Options** and is the version that gets installed.

Settings → "Libraries" now has a filter box for each library list ("Libraries To Register" and
"Libraries To Download"), so a long list of installed libraries can be narrowed down by path or
git repository instead of scrolling.

The chat sidebar's "MCP servers" dropdown lists loaded node libraries that come with their own
tools under "Libraries". Picking one gives the agent those tools for the conversation. Needs
engine 0.107.0 or later.

Dropping a connection on a `ParameterList` handle that does not accept the dragged type now shows
a short warning naming the accepted types, instead of attempting the connection.

A list entry that holds a whole connected list now shows a list icon and, once the upstream node
has run, its item count, so it is no longer mistaken for a single item.

The run toolbar's **Cancel Run** button shows a count of the runs waiting their turn: behind the
run in progress, or in line on another computer your workflow sends nodes to. Hover it to see
them in the order they will start. Needs an engine that queues runs.

The refresh button on the Workflows page also re-checks registered projects, so projects on a
drive that mounted after the engine started show up without restarting the engine. Needs engine
0.107.0 or later.

Expired license keys can be reissued from Admin Dashboard → "License Keys" with a new
expiration date, which reactivates them and keeps their access groups and permission templates.
**Add Parameter → Type → Sequence** declares an image-sequence parameter.

Custom widgets can declare `synced_parameters`. The widget reads those parameters' values and
commits to them directly, so a node no longer copies them into the widget's own value. Dragging
the widget moves the parameters' controls live, scrubbing a synced number or color parameter moves
the widget, and parameters with an incoming connection are locked. Needs an engine that sends
`synced_parameters`.

**Breaking:** The editor needs engine 0.107.0 or later and asks you to update older engines
instead of connecting. From 0.107.0 the engine names itself on every reply, which the editor
needs to know which engine holds a restored session.

The hosted editor finds engines through the Griptape Cloud engine registry instead of engine
heartbeats, so the engine picker shows only the selected organization's engines.

A selected Dot node's ports are larger, so wires can be dragged to and from them without
zooming in.

The Libraries modal's filter now matches a library's description, file path, and git repository
as well as its name, so a library can be found by where it came from or what it does.

In Library Management, "Reset" now shows on the row of any library marked "Problems" or "Failed
to load", next to that label, so it no longer takes expanding the row to find it. Links in a
library's problem details now open in the browser.

The "Reissue token" button on Admin Dashboard → "License Keys" now asks for confirmation before
replacing an active key's token, and can set a new expiration date at the same time.

Clicking "+" or "−" on a list entry, or dropping a connection on a list, now updates the node
right away, with a dimmed placeholder entry and a dashed edge, instead of waiting for the engine
to answer, which was slow on a distant engine. Removing a connected entry also removes its edge
immediately.

The editor now lazy loads heavy components, like the 3D and splat viewers, the image, crop, and
mask editors, and Arrange Graph, the first time you use them.

Every `ParameterList` and `ParameterGroup` header (such as the OpenAI Image Generation node's
"Input Images" list) now shows its collapse chevron on the right instead of the left, and its
connection handle stays visible on the left in both the collapsed and expanded states, including
on an empty list with no items yet. The same handle accepts a single item or a whole list in one
drop, adding each as a new entry labelled with its source while connected (for example "Load
Image · image"), so you
no longer connect through the separate "Add Item" row. To add an empty entry without a connection,
click the "+" at the bottom of the list. It appears only on lists whose entries you can fill in:
text, numbers, true/false, dict and JSON. Other lists, such as Create List and Create Image List,
now gain entries only through connections. A dropped list adds its items to the list instead of
replacing it, so you can connect several lists. A list that can hold any type, such as Create
List, keeps a dropped list as one item. With an engine older than 0.107.0, a dropped single
item still becomes a new entry, but a dropped list connects to the list itself, as before. The
handle keeps its "ready for another connection" look (not a filled, "used up" dot) after the
first drop, since it keeps accepting more.
Removing an entry's connection now leaves the entry in place, collapsed or not, so the list keeps
its order. Previously an entry in a collapsed list was deleted along with its connection.

In the chat sidebar, opening a thread whose last run used a model, provider, or MCP server that
is no longer available now shows a warning icon beside the model picker, once. Clicking it names
the thread and says what each setting switched to; the switch is kept as that thread's setting.
It no longer repeats on every visit and engine start, and clears when you dismiss it or pick new
settings. A retired model with a set replacement moves to it without a warning.

The choice list on a parameter that allows custom values no longer closes when you drag its
scrollbar.

The minus button on a connection removes it immediately. It used to sometimes do nothing until you
clicked elsewhere, because it relied on simulated clicks and key presses.

Digits in the editor no longer render dimmed and spaced out (`PXR24` as `PXR 2 4`) on Linux machines
without any of the default UI fonts installed.
A node dragged over a Dot node now covers the Dot, the same way it covers the Dot's wires.

The editor no longer re-renders every 5 seconds when the engine checks in with nothing new to
report, which removes a periodic stutter, worst on canvases with 3D nodes.

File browser errors, such as a folder that can't be opened or a rename that fails, now show the
engine's reason instead of a generic "Failed to …" message.

The file browser now shows the error when the first folder it opens can't be read, such as a
permission error, instead of spinning forever.

The file browser now keeps the sort you chose when you open another folder, instead of resetting
the listing to folders first.

When a path the file browser tries to open no longer exists, it now falls back to the parent
folder instead of jumping to the root.

"New File" and "New Directory" in the file browser now pick a name that doesn't clash with the
items in the folder you are viewing, instead of one chosen from the previous folder's items.

In Model Management, completed entries under "Downloads" now show an X ("Clear from list")
instead of a red trash icon, since clearing one leaves the model installed, and a "Clear completed"
button clears them all. Active and paused downloads show a stop icon ("Cancel download").

The right-hand Sidebar Panels region no longer sometimes renders blank with an unresponsive panel
toggle after collapsing and re-expanding it, dragging its resize separator, or returning to the
editor after navigating away (e.g. in the desktop app).

After pressing Escape to close the variable picker in a text input, typing inside the same `{`
no longer reopens it on every keystroke.

The workflow browser now remembers the sort you picked (column and direction) for each section,
instead of going back to "Modified" newest first every time it reopens.
License users can connect through Griptape Cloud to engines on other machines that use the same license.
The bundled version of the Griptape Nodes app has been updated to `0.104.0`, with engine `0.108.0` and editor `0.130.0`.

When you sign in with a Griptape account, the app now connects straight to the engine on your computer instead of going through Griptape Cloud. Engines on other machines are still reached through Griptape Cloud.
Only the engine you're connected to can be renamed from **Manage Engines**.
The **Direct Engine WebSocket URL** setting is now shown for every account, since the app always uses it to reach the engine on your computer.

The editor now comes from the engine you're using. The engine on your computer serves its own matching editor, and engines on other machines open in the latest Griptape Nodes web editor, so the editor always fits the engine it's connected to.
When the engine rejects the license at startup, the error now explains the issue and offers a shortcut to license settings.
The Admin Dashboard window no longer always shows horizontal and vertical scrollbars, or an empty band at the top on Linux.
GPU usage and VRAM in the system resources panel no longer stay at N/A for the rest of the session after `nvidia-smi` fails once, such as during a GPU out-of-memory error.

A request envelope (`EventRequest`, and each request in an `EventRequestBatch`) now has an optional
`open_workflow_id` beside `request_id`, naming the open workflow the request runs in.
`EventManager.handle_request` and `ahandle_request` read it from `result_context`, as they read
`request_id`, and echo it on the result envelope, where it stays apart from any `workflow_id` in
the result itself. A request that acts on a workflow fails with `WorkflowNotOpenResultFailure`
without running when its `open_workflow_id` names no open workflow, and with
`WorkflowNotNamedResultFailure` when it leaves the id out while none or several are open; requests
about the engine, such as `EngineHeartbeatRequest`, ignore it. See
[Transports](https://github.com/griptape-ai/griptape-nodes-engine/blob/HEAD/docs/guides/transports.md#sending-requests).

Execution events, such as the current node, parameter value updates and a run's end, and streamed
progress events now have a `workflow_id` naming the open workflow they belong to. A result's
`open_workflow_id` now names the workflow the request acted on even when the request left it out,
such as the only open workflow, a run's own workflow, or the workflow a load opened. See
[Transports](https://github.com/griptape-ai/griptape-nodes-engine/blob/HEAD/docs/guides/transports.md#getting-results-back).

A `FileFormat` trait marks a parameter's value as a file format of a given kind (`image`, `video`,
`audio`, `threed`). It renders the kind as the `file_format` UI option, which the editor copies onto
a Start Flow parameter and the workflow shape reports, so a host running the workflow can offer only
the formats it can open.
[#6193](https://github.com/griptape-ai/griptape-nodes-engine/issues/6193)

`File`, `FileDestination`, `Directory` and `FileSequence` now keep the workflow they were built in,
or take one as `workflow`, so node code that writes from a `threading.Thread` or thread pool
resolves `{outputs}` in the node's workflow. `ProjectFileDestination.from_situation_in_workflow`
does the same for a situation.

`EngineHeartbeatResultSuccess` now reports `engine_run_id`, which changes every time the engine
starts. Workflow ids last only until a restart, so a client that sees a new `engine_run_id` drops
the workflow ids it kept. Unlike `session_id`, it never survives a restart.

`EngineHeartbeatResultSuccess` now lists every open workflow in `open_workflows`. The
`current_workflow` fields describe the one opened last.

Advanced libraries can offer their own request types as tools on the engine's MCP server by
returning them from `get_mcp_tools()`. The chat sidebar lists loaded libraries with tools under
"Libraries" in the "MCP servers" dropdown.

A list parameter's element details now include `row_input_types`, the types a new entry accepts,
even when the list has no entries yet. An editor can use it instead of copying the engine's rules.

MCP clients can now name the workflow their tool calls act on with an `X-Griptape-Workflow-Id`
header. A client that sends none works, for the rest of its MCP session, on the workflow its own
`EnsureWorkflowAndFlowRequest` or `SetWorkflowContextRequest` opened or selected. Either keeps
reaching the workflow after saving a Griptape-provided template continues it in a copy. The
editor's chat agent, including the tools libraries give it, acts on the workflow its message was
sent from. See [Connect External MCP Clients](https://github.com/griptape-ai/griptape-nodes-engine/blob/HEAD/docs/guides/mcp/external_clients.md#choose-the-workflow).

Nodes now have a read-only `workflow` property naming the workflow they were added to, or `None`
for a node that was never added to one, such as during its `__init__`.

`RefreshProjectTemplatesRequest` re-checks every path in `projects_to_register` and loads the
projects that have become reachable since the engine started, such as projects on a network drive
that mounted late, without restarting the engine.
[#6134](https://github.com/griptape-ai/griptape-nodes-engine/issues/6134)

Every request result now carries `engine_id` on its envelope, naming the engine that sent it, so
a client that reaches an engine through a session topic knows which engine holds the session.

The sidebar agent leaves out a skill whose `SKILL.md` frontmatter sets
`disable-model-invocation: true`, so a skill can stay in `.agents/skills` without the agent
using it.

The engine log now warns when a skill's `description` is longer than 1,024 characters or its
frontmatter sets fields that Griptape Nodes ignores, such as `allowed-tools`.

The `Widget` trait takes a `synced_parameters` list naming other parameters on the node that a
custom widget reads and writes directly, so a node no longer copies them into the widget's own
value. See
[Custom Widgets](https://docs.griptapenodes.com/en/stable/development/custom_nodes/custom_widgets/).
[#4639](https://github.com/griptape-ai/griptape-nodes-engine/issues/4639)

Every workflow now has a `workflow_id` that the engine gives it while it runs. It stays the same
when the workflow is saved, renamed, or moved, and when the engine rescans the workspace, but it
is not saved in the workflow's file, so a restarted engine gives the workflow a new one. Results
that name a workflow now also report its id, such as `GetWorkflowContextSuccess.workflow_id` and
`EngineHeartbeatResultSuccess.current_workflow_id`.

**Breaking:** A saved workflow file's `build_workflow()` no longer opens a workflow. It builds into
the workflow its caller opened, and `aexecute_workflow()` opens the file when it runs on its own.
Code that runs a saved file by awaiting `build_workflow()` directly must open the workflow first
with `GriptapeNodes.ContextManager().push_workflow(file_path=...)`, or call
`GriptapeNodes.WorkflowManager().run_workflow()`, which opens it when none is open. Files saved
before keep working unchanged.

**Breaking:** `SetWorkflowContextRequest` and `EnsureWorkflowAndFlowRequest` now open a new
unsaved workflow only from a `workflow_name` of `unsaved:` followed by 32 lowercase hex digits,
the form the engine mints. Any other `unsaved:` name fails. Leave `workflow_name` out to have the
engine pick one, and read it from the result.

**Breaking:** The `Workflow` class in `griptape_nodes.node_library.workflow_registry` changed for
node libraries that use it. `Workflow.file_path` is read-only: move a workflow's file with
`MoveWorkflowRequest`. The constructor now takes a `workflow_id`, and `Workflow.from_disk` is
gone: register a workflow file with `RegisterWorkflowRequest`. The registry's
`clear_all_workflows` is gone: rescan the workspace with `RefreshWorkflowRegistryRequest`.

**Breaking:** `SetWorkflowContextRequest` and `EnsureWorkflowAndFlowRequest` now fail for a
`workflow_name` that no registered workflow has, instead of opening a blank workflow under that
name. To start a new workflow, leave `workflow_name` out and pass `display_name`.
`ContextManager.push_workflow(workflow_name=...)` with such a name opens a new unsaved workflow
with that display name and returns its `unsaved:<id>` name. `push_workflow(file_path=...)` with a
path that has no file opens a new unsaved workflow in that file's folder, whose `absolute_path` on
`ContextManager.get_current_workflow()` is `None`.

**Breaking:** `RunWorkflowFromRegistryRequest` with `run_with_clean_slate=False` now fails while
a workflow is open, instead of loading the second workflow into the open one, since only one
workflow is open at a time. Clear the open workflow first with `ClearAllObjectStateRequest`, or
send `run_with_clean_slate=True`. Likewise, `GriptapeNodes.ContextManager().push_workflow()` and
its `workflow()` block now refuse while a workflow is open.

A list parameter connected to a whole list now keeps its own entries. The node reads the
connected list's items first, then the entries added by hand, instead of ignoring the entries.

"Add Library" now downloads only a library's metadata file when inspecting a Git repository,
instead of every file in the latest commit. Repositories with large files inspect much faster,
especially on slow connections.
[#4836](https://github.com/griptape-ai/griptape-nodes-engine/issues/4836)

`MergeWorkflowBranchRequest` now fails while the branch or its source is the open workflow. The
merge removes the branch and rewrites the source's file, which the open workflow's next save
would write over. Open another workflow first.

Creating a global variable with `CreateVariableRequest` now fails when no workflow is open,
instead of storing it for the whole engine.

The library warning about components older than the ones Griptape Nodes runs on now suggests
resetting the library when those versions are left over from an earlier install, and links to a
new troubleshooting section in the Libraries guide.
[#6098](https://github.com/griptape-ai/griptape-nodes-engine/issues/6098)

The sidebar agent now reads a skill's bundled files with read-only file tools, so it can look
through the skill's folder and read scripts, images, and PDFs as well as text. It still can't run
scripts.

A node whose library runs in a separate process now fails with "no workflow was open when it was
sent" when its `ExecuteNodeRequest` names no open workflow (`orchestrator_workflow_id`), instead of
running outside any workflow. Running a node from an open workflow always names it.

The `WorkflowRegistry` classmethods `generate_new_workflow`, `ensure_unsaved`,
`delete_workflow_by_name`, `clear_user_workflows`, and `rekey_workflow` are deprecated and log a
warning when called. They will be removed in 0.110.0. Use `RegisterWorkflowRequest`,
`SetWorkflowContextRequest`, `DeleteWorkflowRequest`, `RefreshWorkflowRegistryRequest`, and
`MoveWorkflowRequest` or `RenameWorkflowRequest` instead.

**Breaking:** Manager methods that acted on whichever workflow was open are removed. Call the `_in`
variant with the node's workflow, for example `FlowManager.get_parent_flow_in(self.workflow, name)`.
`cancel_flow_run` becomes `cancel_all_runs_in(workflow)`, and the `ContextManager` path getters
become `absolute_path` and `working_directory` on `get_current_workflow()`.
`FlowManager.cancel_run` now requires `flows`; use `cancel_run_in(workflow, run_id)`.
Removed: `ObjectManager.add_object_by_name`, `del_obj_by_name`; `FlowManager.get_parent_flow`,
`reparent_flow`, `flow_state`, `unresolve_all_nodes_in_flow`, `clear_execution_queue`,
`cancel_flow_run`, `has_connection`, `get_connections_on_node`, `get_connected_output_parameters`,
`get_connected_input_parameters`, `get_connected_input_from_node`,
`get_connected_output_from_node`, `get_start_node_queue`, `get_start_node_from_node`,
`get_prev_node`; `ContextManager.get_current_workflow_file_path`,
`get_current_workflow_working_directory`.

The File Browser dialog's file preview no longer sends the entire file as a data URL for images
over 10 MB that Pillow can't decode, which could hang the engine base64-encoding a large or
multi-part sequence frame (e.g. EXR). Those files now get no preview instead. Images Pillow can
decode still get a thumbnail regardless of file size.

A data node fed by a ForEach or ForLoop Start's `current_item` or `index` now re-evaluates on every
pass of every run, not only the first. On later runs it kept its value from the last pass of the
previous run and fed it to every pass.
[#5751](https://github.com/griptape-ai/griptape-nodes-engine/issues/5751)

`InspectLibraryRepoRequest` now honors a `url@ref` suffix on `git_url` (for example
`user/repo@stable`), as `DownloadLibraryRequest` already does, instead of failing to reach the
repository. `ref` is now optional and overrides the suffix when set.

Inspecting a library from a Git repository in the Add Library modal no longer blocks the engine
while the repository is fetched, which could drop the editor's connection on Windows.
[#4836](https://github.com/griptape-ai/griptape-nodes-engine/issues/4836)

Saving or copying a node keeps the item types of its lists. A list whose type a node set while
running, such as Display List's, loads as `list[Thing]` instead of `list[list[Thing]]`, and a row
the node typed on its own, such as an `int` row beside `str` rows, keeps its value instead of
failing to load. Workflows saved before this fix still load their list types as saved.

A data node fed by a node that runs again now recomputes instead of passing on its earlier
output. Before, pressing Run a second time, or a later pass of a For Loop or For Each group,
could hand the next node the previous run's value: for example, Merge Texts kept its first
result while the Agent feeding it wrote new text.

While, Retry and For Each groups now end, repeat, skip or break the loop according to the branch
the loop body took. Before, a node on a branch that was not taken could still run, and its exit
then counted as taken: a group whose body reached "Done" could run again, and a For Each group
whose body reached "Loop Complete" could break out of the loop.
When several body nodes are wired into the same exit, every wire is now checked, not only the
first one drawn, so the result no longer depends on the order the connections were made.

A loop no longer counts the entries of a list twice when the list is also connected as a whole
list. After the loop ran, the list read, and saved, its own entries a second time.

A data node with no control connections that reads, directly or through other data nodes, from a
node on the control path now shows this run's value when the workflow is run again. Before, in
"parallel" execution mode it could keep the previous run's value, or read a blank value, because
it ran at the same time as the node feeding it.

Renaming the open workflow no longer closes it and reloads it from its file, so its canvas and
node results are no longer reset. It stays open under the new name.

Resolving a node downstream of a `ForEach` loop while the loop is still running no longer leaves
the workflow stuck as running. The downstream node now runs once the loop finishes, and later
runs of it are no longer refused with "already executing".
[#5754](https://github.com/griptape-ai/griptape-nodes-engine/issues/5754)

Resolving a node that reads a `ForEach` or `ForLoop` End's `results`, after editing an input to
the loop body, now runs the loop again and finishes. Before, the loop never started, the body ran
once outside the loop with a stale `current_item`, and the resolved node stayed running forever.

Running a node placed after a `ForEach` loop no longer fails with a `KeyError` naming a node from
outside the loop, once every iteration has finished, when a node in the loop body reads an input
from that outside node. The run now completes and the node after the loop gets every iteration's
results. Other nodes outside the loop that read the same outside node, such as a `Display Text`,
now show this run's value instead of the previous run's.
[#5753](https://github.com/griptape-ai/griptape-nodes-engine/issues/5753)
[#5747](https://github.com/griptape-ai/griptape-nodes-engine/issues/5747)
Images in nodes no longer stay blank, or keep pulsing, after a run or a reload. This happened when the app rejoined its previous session before Griptape Cloud listed that session.

`claude-haiku-5-5` is available in Griptape Cloud model dropdowns and the chat sidebar, with
image input. [#5987](https://github.com/griptape-ai/griptape-nodes-engine/issues/5987)

`DescribeNodeTypeRequest` now reports each parameter's `element_type` and, for a `ParameterList`, its
`max_items`, so clients can tell multi-input parameters from plain list inputs without creating a node.
[#5918](https://github.com/griptape-ai/griptape-nodes-engine/issues/5918)

A library's nodes can now run on another computer's Griptape Nodes engine while you keep working
in your own editor. Several people can share that computer: it runs one person's run at a time,
frees the previous person's models when it passes to the next, and the run toolbar shows a run
that waits for it as queued. See
[Running Nodes on Another Computer](https://docs.griptapenodes.com/en/stable/guides/run_nodes_on_another_computer/).

Node libraries can read the inputs and outputs of an imported workflow's flow with
`GetWorkflowShapeRequest`, which also works from a node running in a worker.
[griptape-nodes-library-standard#883](https://github.com/griptape-ai/griptape-nodes-library-standard/issues/883)

`LoadMetadataForAllLibrariesRequest` now takes `include_git_info`. Pass `false` to skip the git
lookups behind `git_remote` and `git_ref`, which take several git processes per library, when
only the library schemas are needed.
[#5943](https://github.com/griptape-ai/griptape-nodes-engine/issues/5943)

MCP clients can now call `GetFlowSummaryRequest` to see a flow's nodes, the values set on them,
their multi-inputs, and their connections in one compact request, instead of
`ListNodesInFlowRequest` and a full `GetAllNodeInfoRequest` per node. Outputs, run results, and UI
state are left out. [#5967](https://github.com/griptape-ai/griptape-nodes-engine/issues/5967)

Model downloads can be paused with `PauseModelDownloadRequest` and resumed with
`ResumeModelDownloadRequest`, and stay paused across engine restarts. Resuming skips files that
already finished. Nodes won't run on a paused or failed download.
[#4563](https://github.com/griptape-ai/griptape-nodes-engine/issues/4563)

Three strict-mode rules flag node code that behaves differently in a separate process than
in-process: `graph-access-while-loading` (asking about connections or other nodes while the node
loads), `state-read-bypassing-requests` (reading a manager instead of sending a request), and
`state-outside-parameters` (keeping state set by `after_value_set` or a connection hook on the
node instead of in a parameter). Each warns where the node runs in-process and fails the node's run
in a separate process.
[#5955](https://github.com/griptape-ai/griptape-nodes-engine/issues/5955)

`validate_empty_parameter()` takes a `skip_if_connected` option for use in
`validate_before_workflow_run`, which runs before connections deliver their values. With it, a
parameter that a connection feeds is not reported as blank.
[#5889](https://github.com/griptape-ai/griptape-nodes-engine/issues/5889)

**Breaking:** A node whose library runs in a separate process now runs there on a copy loaded the
way a saved workflow reopens, with the same parameters and types as the node in the editor,
including parameters added in the editor, by requests, and by its value hooks. `after_value_set`
no longer runs in that process, and nothing the node's code sends while the copy loads reaches the
workflow. A node whose `process` relied on state its `after_value_set` set needs to keep that
state in a parameter; see
[Node Isolation with Workers](https://github.com/griptape-ai/griptape-nodes-engine/blob/HEAD/docs/development/custom_nodes/node_isolation_with_workers.md#the-rules-that-keep-a-worker-identical-to-running-in-process).
[#5955](https://github.com/griptape-ai/griptape-nodes-engine/issues/5955)

The built-in chat now starts each message with the available node types and the current flow, so
it builds a change in one `EventRequestBatch` call instead of first making discovery calls.
[#5909](https://github.com/griptape-ai/griptape-nodes-engine/issues/5909)

`StartFlowRequest`, `StartFlowFromNodeRequest`, and `ResolveNodeRequest` sent while another run
is in progress now wait for that run to finish and then start, instead of failing with "Flow is
already running". Waiting runs start in the order they were sent, and a new `RunQueuedEvent` tells
the editor each waiting run's place in line, with the `request_id` of the request that submitted
it. Their results now carry the run's `run_id`. The new `ListRunsRequest` lists the run in
progress and the waiting runs, `CancelRunRequest` withdraws a waiting run or stops the run in
progress, and `CancelAllRunsRequest` cancels every run. Running a node while another node is
running still adds it to that run, as before.

A node's `validate_before_node_run` now runs in a worker thread instead of on the engine's event
loop, so a slow check, such as reading a large or remote file, no longer freezes the editor and
other flows while it runs. The node still waits for its own checks before it runs, and a failed
check stops the run as before.
[#5963](https://github.com/griptape-ai/griptape-nodes-engine/issues/5963)

Workflow nodes that import their workflows at the same time, in parallel branches or in a loop
set to "Run Group Items All at Once", no longer mix up which workflow each node's flow came from.
Before, a node's flow could be saved as a reference to another node's workflow.
[#5665](https://github.com/griptape-ai/griptape-nodes-engine/issues/5665)

In a reopened workflow, removing or replacing a connection into a parameter its node rebuilt while
loading, such as a ControlNet's provider settings, no longer fails with "Connection does not
exist". Deleting that node no longer fails either. A connection into a parameter its node no
longer has can also be removed, along with both of its nodes and their flow.

A `ForEach Group`, `For Loop Group`, or `Retry Group` no longer fails to start with "Failed while
restoring the saved value of '<node>.<parameter>'" when a body node's connected input holds a value
that its own range no longer allows, such as a crop coordinate left over from a wider image. The
loop body copy now leaves out values that its connections supply, in both execution modes. As a
result, a body node's `validate_before_workflow_run` sees a connected input's default rather than
the value shown on the canvas, the same as a node at the top level of the workflow.
[#5889](https://github.com/griptape-ai/griptape-nodes-engine/issues/5889)

A list fed by a connection keeps its items when its node is pasted together with the node feeding
it, instead of coming back empty until that node runs again.
[#5955](https://github.com/griptape-ai/griptape-nodes-engine/issues/5955)

Setting a parameter that has a hard-limited slider or a min/max range to `None` no longer fails
with "'>' not supported between instances of 'NoneType' and 'float'". `None` passed over a
connection into an optional number parameter now goes through instead of stopping the flow.
[#6063](https://github.com/griptape-ai/griptape-nodes-engine/issues/6063)

A restarted model download no longer shows progress from 0%. Files finished on an earlier
attempt now count as downloaded and toward the total.
[#6087](https://github.com/griptape-ai/griptape-nodes-engine/issues/6087)

When a saved value cannot be restored while a workflow or loop body is rebuilt, the error now
includes the reason, such as "must be between 0 and 50", instead of only naming the parameter.
[#5889](https://github.com/griptape-ai/griptape-nodes-engine/issues/5889)

Griptape Nodes Engine is pinned to 0.106.0. See its
[release notes](https://github.com/griptape-ai/griptape-nodes-engine/releases/tag/v0.106.0).
`gtn diagnostics collect` now runs. The command was documented but missing from `gtn`.

Engine processes now read `GTN_APPEND_PYTHONPATH`, a list of folders added to the end of the
module search path. Modules in those folders can be imported from nodes, but never replace the
engine's own packages the way `PYTHONPATH` entries can.

`CreateConnectionResultSuccess` now has a `replaced_connection` field, and its message names the
connection, when the new connection replaced one on an input or control output that allows only
one connection.
[#5912](https://github.com/griptape-ai/griptape-nodes-engine/issues/5912)

`CreateNodeResultSuccess` now has a `paired_node_name` field naming the End node that creating
a For Each or For Loop Start node also creates, so clients don't create a second one.
[#5911](https://github.com/griptape-ai/griptape-nodes-engine/issues/5911)

A `DatePicker` trait gives a `str` parameter a calendar picker in the editor. The value is an
ISO 8601 local date such as `2026-10-14`, or `2026-10-14T09:30` with `include_time=True`, so a
node can read it with `date.fromisoformat`. Optional `min` and `max` bound the allowed dates.
[#5890](https://github.com/griptape-ai/griptape-nodes-engine/issues/5890)

Nodes that call a model provider directly, rather than through Griptape Cloud, can now take part
in Griptape Cloud spending budgets. `BudgetAccessRequest` asks Cloud before the call and fails
with the same "Budget stopped this run." message when a budget refuses it; if Cloud cannot be
reached the call goes ahead. `ReportUsageRequest` sends the call's token counts afterwards, in the
background, and Cloud prices them. See [Budgets for Direct Provider Calls](https://docs.griptapenodes.com/en/stable/development/custom_nodes/direct_provider_budgets/).
[#5422](https://github.com/griptape-ai/griptape-nodes-engine/issues/5422)

An "Isolated Execution in a worker" beta feature runs the nodes of groups and loops set to
"Isolated Execution" in one background process that stays open for the session, instead of
starting a new process each time the group or loop runs. The group's results no longer travel
through Griptape Cloud, so Isolated Execution works on installs that can't reach it. Turn it on
from the editor's Beta settings page.

Advanced libraries can return execution and app event listeners from
`get_execution_event_listeners()` and `get_app_event_listeners()`, for example to log or time
every node a workflow runs. The engine registers them when the library loads and removes them
when it unloads. See the
[timing example](https://github.com/griptape-ai/griptape-nodes-engine/blob/HEAD/docs/development/custom_nodes/advanced_libraries.md#example-a-library-that-times-every-node-run).
[#5779](https://github.com/griptape-ai/griptape-nodes-engine/issues/5779)

Each `successful_libraries` entry from `LoadMetadataForAllLibrariesRequest` now reports how the
engine's last attempt to load that library went, as `lifecycle_state`, `fitness`, `problems`,
and `execution_env_failure`, so a library that failed to load can be told apart from one waiting
for a refresh.
[#5102](https://github.com/griptape-ai/griptape-nodes-engine/issues/5102)

`ListNodeTypesInLibraryRequest` takes `include_metadata` to also return each node type's category,
display name, description, and deprecation. MCP clients can survey every library's node types in
one `EventRequestBatch` instead of reading library manifests off the engine's disk. It reads library
metadata only, so it loads no node code.
[#5962](https://github.com/griptape-ai/griptape-nodes-engine/issues/5962)

New setting `max_loop_iterations_in_parallel` limits how many iterations of a loop set to
"Run Group Items All at Once" run at the same time. Defaults to 0 (no limit).
[#5067](https://github.com/griptape-ai/griptape-nodes-engine/issues/5067)

MCP clients can now call `CancelFlowRequest` to stop a running flow and `UnresolveFlowRequest` to
reset a flow's nodes, so an agent can recover a stuck run without reloading the workflow.
[#5754](https://github.com/griptape-ai/griptape-nodes-engine/issues/5754)

MCP clients can now call `ValidateFlowDependenciesRequest` to run a flow's pre-run checks without
running it, so an agent can find wiring and configuration errors before spending a run on them.
[#5917](https://github.com/griptape-ai/griptape-nodes-engine/issues/5917)

Node libraries can build a `NodeError` for a failed provider call with `NodeError.from_missing_secret`,
`NodeError.from_http_response` and `NodeError.from_request_exception`, instead of each library
writing its own helpers. A refused API key links to the secret in Settings, and timeouts and
failed connections get a plain message.
[#5899](https://github.com/griptape-ai/griptape-nodes-engine/issues/5899)

`NodeStartProcessEvent` is sent again before every node runs, and `NodeFinishProcessEvent` after,
for every node the engine runs: regular nodes, nodes that run in a worker, group and loop nodes,
and the nodes inside them. Both now carry `node_type`, `specific_library_name`, `flow_name`,
`execution_id`, and `parent_execution_id`, and `NodeFinishProcessEvent` says how the run ended
(`outcome`, `error_message`, `error`). Loop body nodes are named as on the canvas.
[#5779](https://github.com/griptape-ai/griptape-nodes-engine/issues/5779)

`ParameterList` takes `item_converters`, which convert each item whether it is set in its own row
or arrives in a whole list. A whole list a node sets on its own list with `set_parameter_value`
now becomes the list's items, as it does when set by request. See
[Parameters](https://github.com/griptape-ai/griptape-nodes-engine/blob/HEAD/docs/development/custom_nodes/parameters.md).

The engine now watches each local file the editor previews and sends a `StaticFileChanged` event
when the file is saved, including saves from other apps, so the editor can show the new content.
Turn it off with the `refresh_previews_on_file_change` setting, and cap how many files are watched
with `refresh_previews_max_files` (1000 by default).

`ResetLibraryRequest` deletes a library's Python environments (`.venv` and `.venv-exec`) and
builds them again, so a library whose packages are broken can be recovered without deleting
folders by hand. When the engine has already loaded packages from the library, the reset finishes
the next time the engine starts and the result reports `restart_required`.
`LoadMetadataForAllLibrariesRequest` reports `reset_requires_restart` so a client can say so
before the reset is confirmed.
[#5102](https://github.com/griptape-ai/griptape-nodes-engine/issues/5102)

**Breaking:** The chat agent now asks before it runs workflows or nodes, generates images, or uses
tools from your own MCP servers, so a question no longer spends credits unprompted. Such a turn
ends `RunAgentRequest` with the calls in `output.pending_approvals` instead of running them, and
they run only once a client answers with `ResolveToolApprovalsRequest`; see
[Approvals](https://github.com/griptape-ai/griptape-nodes-engine/blob/HEAD/docs/guides/agent/approvals.md).
[#5606](https://github.com/griptape-ai/griptape-nodes-engine/issues/5606)

**Breaking:** The "Private Execution" option for groups and loops is now called "Isolated
Execution": it runs them in a separate process, which keeps them apart but does not make them
private. Workflows saved with "Private Execution" open with "Isolated Execution" selected. A
workflow saved after this change opens in an older version with "Local Execution" selected. Node
libraries that import `PRIVATE_EXECUTION` from `griptape_nodes.exe_types.node_types` need to use
`ISOLATED_EXECUTION` instead.

Opening, pasting, and editing large workflows spend less time after each request as the workflow
grows. The engine used to check every node for pending editor updates after each request; it now
checks only the nodes that changed.

The editor no longer stalls while the engine saves a large image with its workflow metadata or
makes an image preview.

Loading libraries, at engine startup and on a library reload or project switch, no longer runs
git several times per library or re-reads every package installed in the engine's environment.
With three libraries installed, a reload takes about 0.2 seconds instead of 1.9.
[#5940](https://github.com/griptape-ai/griptape-nodes-engine/issues/5940)

A `NodeError` response over 16 KB now keeps its structure, with base64 data replaced by its length
and strings over 2000 characters cut, instead of being dropped. It is dropped only if it is still
too large.
[#5899](https://github.com/griptape-ai/griptape-nodes-engine/issues/5899)

Running a workflow spends less time between nodes. Before each node runs, the engine reads the
project's variables, and it now works out `{workflow_dir}` once per read instead of once for
every project directory.

The sidebar agent no longer fails with "Request timed out" behind proxies that hold the TLS
handshake for longer than 5 seconds. Model requests now allow 60 seconds to connect.
[#5768](https://github.com/griptape-ai/griptape-nodes-engine/issues/5768)

A chat message that reaches the agent's limit on steps per message no longer disappears from the
conversation with an error. The agent's work up to the limit stays in the conversation, and the
reply says it stopped, so sending "continue" picks up where it left off.
[#5908](https://github.com/griptape-ai/griptape-nodes-engine/issues/5908)

Griptape Cloud storage and file requests now keep the path in `GT_CLOUD_BASE_URL`. A base URL like
`https://example.com/prefix` sent requests to `https://example.com/api/...`, dropping `/prefix`.
[#5789](https://github.com/griptape-ai/griptape-nodes-engine/issues/5789)

A value that reaches a node over a connection is no longer run through variable substitution
again when the node copies it onto its own output. A save node's `Saved to: {outputs}/a.mp4`
status wired into an End node now stays a macro on the End node too, so the saved workflow
holds no absolute path. [#5897](https://github.com/griptape-ai/griptape-nodes-engine/issues/5897)

The `execution_events` panel of a group set to Isolated Execution or to a library's environment
no longer shows every event twice. It shows a "Starting:" line for each node again, and a
"Finished:", "Failed:", or "Cancelled:" line when the node ends.
[#5779](https://github.com/griptape-ai/griptape-nodes-engine/issues/5779)

The engine reports that it is still initializing from the moment it starts, not only once library
loading begins. An editor that connects during startup now waits for the engine instead of
showing a connection error.

Library templates no longer disappear from the editor's library filters after switching
projects. Switching now re-registers each library's templates against the new project.
[#5765](https://github.com/griptape-ai/griptape-nodes-engine/issues/5765)

**Create** on a workflow a library provides now makes a copy in your workspace even when the
library did not mark it `is_template`, and saving an open library workflow writes a copy instead
of overwriting the library's file. Before, **Create** opened the library's own file for editing.

Removing or moving an item of a list parameter now updates the list that
`GetParameterValueRequest` returns, reruns the nodes that read it, and lets the node react, as
"Path Join" does when it recomputes its output. A node whose library runs in a separate process
now receives its list inputs instead of an empty list.

A row of a list parameter (for example `reference_images` on "Kling Omni Video Generation") now
accepts a whole list, such as the output of "Create Image List", and adds its items to the list.

Workflows with a chain of more than about 1,000 connected nodes now run and accept edits. Before,
passing a value down the chain failed with "maximum recursion depth exceeded". Passing values
down long chains also takes less time.

A `ForEach Group`, `For Loop Group`, or `Retry Group` whose body holds a node with a list
parameter wired row by row from other nodes, such as `Merge Images`, no longer fails at the end of
the run with "Attempted to set list ... some of its items are connected to other nodes".
[#6013](https://github.com/griptape-ai/griptape-nodes-engine/issues/6013)

Creating a For Each or For Loop Start node with `CreateNodeRequest` and no `position` in its
`metadata` now creates and connects its End node, instead of failing with `'position'`.
[#5910](https://github.com/griptape-ai/griptape-nodes-engine/issues/5910)

Opening a workflow by running a file the registry doesn't know (for example, one outside the
workspace) no longer shows a "GetWorkflowMetadata Failed" error. Its metadata is read from the
file's header.
[#5794](https://github.com/griptape-ai/griptape-nodes-engine/issues/5794)

A node failing in a parallel run no longer cancels the other nodes running alongside it. Nodes
that already started finish and show their results, nodes still waiting to start are skipped, and
the run then reports the failure. Cancelling a run still stops every node.
[#5893](https://github.com/griptape-ai/griptape-nodes-engine/issues/5893)

A loop set to "Run Group Items All at Once" no longer floods the editor with events about the
temporary copies of its body, which could make the editor report the engine as disconnected.
[#5067](https://github.com/griptape-ai/griptape-nodes-engine/issues/5067)

Switching projects no longer freezes the editor for about 25 seconds and stops a library's nodes
from running for the rest of the session, when that library runs its nodes in a separate process
and the new project's workspace contains saved workflows.
[#5946](https://github.com/griptape-ai/griptape-nodes-engine/issues/5946)

Saving a workflow right after updating one of its libraries now keeps parameter values whose
type comes from that library, such as a node's mode dropdown. Before, the save dropped those
values with a warning, and engines before 0.104.0 failed to save with "Missing stable
namespace".

A node's status no longer has project variables substituted into it during a run, so a status
such as `Saved to: {outputs}/a.mp4` is saved with the workflow as written instead of as the
absolute path. [#5897](https://github.com/griptape-ai/griptape-nodes-engine/issues/5897)

Closing a workflow that contains node groups, such as a ForEach Group, no longer logs a
"subflow doesn't exist" warning for each group.
[#5746](https://github.com/griptape-ai/griptape-nodes-engine/issues/5746)

Setting a whole list on an unconnected list parameter by request (an MCP client, an agent, a
script) now fills the list's items, the same as entering them one by one in the editor. The
request used to succeed while the node still read an empty list.
[#5758](https://github.com/griptape-ai/griptape-nodes-engine/issues/5758)

A node whose library runs in a separate worker process no longer waits up to 10 minutes when
that process stops while starting up, for example because no license session was available
for it. The run now fails right away and says that the process stopped and where to look.

Running a node whose library runs in a separate process no longer deletes connections when the
node reacts to a value by changing its wires, such as `Load Pipeline Component` in the Modular
Diffusion library dropping every wire it fed after a run.

A library whose nodes run in a worker process now starts its worker as soon as the library
finishes installing. Its runs no longer fail with a "No module named" error after a first install
until the engine restarts, and a library installed from Git while the editor is connected no
longer goes without a worker until **Refresh Libraries**.

Workflows behind a library's `workflow_nodes`, such as the Modular Diffusion "Preconfigured"
nodes, are now listed under their library as soon as the library loads. Before, they appeared
only after the node was placed, and a workspace change removed them again.

The engine registry record carries `clients`, the clients listed on the engine's session, so a
discovery client can tell a free engine from one another host is already driving.

Setting `transports.http_direct.enabled` to `true` makes the engine accept requests POSTed to
`/` or `/events` on `127.0.0.1:18126`, answered with `202 Accepted`. Browser pages can call it
from the Griptape Nodes editors and from origins listed in
`transports.http_direct.allowed_origins`.

Each `provenance` entry in a permission denial now carries `authority`, the evaluation authority
the cloud stamped on the policy, plus `is_service_policy`, true for a Griptape platform policy
the organization cannot remove, and `is_org_attached`, true for a Griptape managed policy an
organization administrator attached and can detach.

Griptape Nodes Engine is pinned to 0.105.0. See its
[release notes](https://github.com/griptape-ai/griptape-nodes-engine/releases/tag/v0.105.0).
The editor installed with the `editor` extra is pinned to 0.129.0.

With a license, opening a connection to any transport no longer contacts the license server
while the license session is live. A released seat or an updated license policy now takes effect
at the next session renewal, within a few minutes, instead of on the next connection.

An editor connected through Griptape Cloud now shows the progress bar, logs, and previews of a
node running in a library's worker process while it runs, instead of only its final values,
when the engine also serves `websocket_direct`.

`griptape-nodes` now installs on Python 3.13. Each platform ships one wheel built on Python's
stable ABI, which loads on 3.12 and 3.13, instead of a wheel that loads on 3.12 only.

A request the engine cannot read, such as one whose type comes from a library that is not
installed, is now answered with a `GenericResultFailure` on its `response_topic` instead of
being dropped, so the client gets an error instead of timing out. In an `EventRequestBatch`, an
unreadable request fails on its own and the rest of the batch still runs.

The engine's connection to Griptape Cloud now sends a ping every 20 seconds and reconnects when
one goes unanswered or a send stalls. A connection dropped silently by the network, for example
after sleep or a NAT timeout, no longer leaves the editor unable to reach a running engine.

Griptape Cloud engine discovery no longer lists a library's worker processes. Workers accept no
client connections, so a client that picked one from the list timed out connecting to it.
Engine records no longer include `orchestrator_engine_id`.

A permission denial from a Griptape managed policy that an organization attached to its license
now says an organization administrator can detach it, instead of saying the policy cannot be
overridden by the organization. That wording now appears only for Griptape platform policies.

With a license, an engine whose seat an admin releases now retries for a seat every 30 seconds
during the grace period and keeps running once it gets one, instead of shutting down when the
grace period ends.

With a license set, a client that connects while `gtn` is starting, such as the desktop app,
no longer takes a second license seat. The extra seat stayed counted against the pool for up to
five minutes, and when only one seat was free the engine failed to start with "No sessions
available".

With engine 0.105.0 or later, the sidebar chat agent asks before running a workflow, running a
node, generating an image, or calling an MCP tool, with "Approve once", "Approve for
conversation", and "Deny" on each pending call. Threads that have approved something for the
conversation show an "Allowed in this chat" line with a "Reset" control to clear it.

Parameters with the `DatePicker` trait show a calendar button with the date, or date and time,
in your locale. Days outside the trait's range can't be picked.

Hosts can hide the editor's engine picker by setting `showEnginePicker: false` in the bridge's
iframe config. The desktop app does this because it draws its own engine controls, and the editor
an engine serves itself hides it because that page only ever talks to its own engine.

On the Admin License Keys page, checking several keys now shows Revoke and Delete buttons that act on all
of them after one confirmation, instead of the checkboxes doing nothing.

Audio recording nodes have a microphone picker and show a live waveform while recording. The
editor remembers your microphone on this device and falls back to the default one if it is
unplugged.

Audio players have a new waveform player with volume, playback speed, and a scrubbable waveform.
Drag the waveform to hear that part of the clip.

Library Management now shows libraries that failed to load, with the engine's problem details,
and offers a "Reset" action that clears and rebuilds a library's Python environments while
keeping its files and settings. The confirmation says when the reset will only finish after an
engine restart. "Reset" appears with engine 0.105.0 or later.

Usage Audit has an Export button. It exports every spend record in the page's date range as CSV
or JSON Lines, including spend on your own provider accounts and requests that were refused or
released, and offers the file to download when it's ready.

With the "Controls under minimap" beta feature on, the canvas controls bar uses the same button
style as the main canvas toolbar, and the minimap is as wide as the controls bar.

A selected Dot node's ports are larger, so wires can be dragged to and from them without
zooming in.

The license key expiration field sets the time inside its calendar popup, and shows the chosen
date and time in your locale.

Activating a project from its detail view in Manage Projects now keeps the view open. The
"Activate" button shows a spinner while the switch runs, then becomes the "Active" pill in the
same spot. Other "Activate" buttons are disabled until the switch finishes.

Switching projects from the Load Workflow modal now replaces the workflow list with a loading panel
that shows each step (switching, loading libraries, loading workflows) until the new project's
workflows are ready, instead of leaving the old list clickable under a progress banner that could
get stuck or reappear after the switch. The "Switching to…" and "Switched to…" toasts are gone.

Running a workflow no longer re-renders every node on the canvas each time a node starts or
finishes, so large workflows stay responsive while they run.

Streaming output into a node, such as an agent response, no longer re-renders every
parameter on that node for each token, so long runs keep the canvas responsive.

Dragging a column divider in the Admin Dashboard's License Keys and Access Groups tables moves the
divider with the mouse, including when the table scrolls horizontally.

Creating a workflow from a template no longer shows a "ListFlowsInFlow Failed" error while the
new workflow loads.

Deleting a group no longer leaves duplicate copies of the connections between the nodes that were
inside it.

Activating a project from Manage Projects no longer waits on a full library refresh, so the switch
finishes as fast as it does from the Workflows (File → Open) dialog.

With engine 0.105.0 or later, image, video, and audio previews of local files update as soon as
the file is saved, including edits made in another app, without reloading the editor.

When a node removes a parameter from inside a parameter group, the parameter now disappears from
the node right away instead of staying on screen until the workflow is reloaded.

Panning a large workflow while it runs is smoother. Node updates no longer re-render every
connection on the canvas.

Panning or zooming a large workflow while it runs is smoother. The pulsing and spinning status
indicators on running nodes pause while the canvas moves.

Panning a large workflow while it runs is smoother. Node updates no longer make the canvas
re-check every node, connection and handle several times over.

Tapping empty canvas with a pen or drawing tablet no longer moves the view a few pixels while it
clears the selection. Dragging the pen past a short distance still pans.

Switching projects from the Load Workflow modal no longer re-sends the workflow list, library
metadata, workflow info and thumbnail requests several times, and thumbnails no longer carry over
from the previous project. The workflow list now asks the engine only for the fields the table
shows, and a branch's status is checked when its row is shown, not for every branch on load.

Read-only text in a rich text input, single-line or multi-line (an Agent's output, say), can be
selected and copied again.

Recording from a stereo microphone now saves both channels. Before, the saved WAV could be
corrupt. Leaving a node mid-recording also now stops the microphone instead of leaving it open.

The unsaved-changes asterisk next to the workflow name in the header stays visible when a long
name is truncated.

In Usage Audit's Per Model view, the spend chart's axis labels and dots stay the same size as the
rest of the page on wide windows instead of growing with the panel.
Image parameters marked for webcam capture show the camera again instead of an upload box.

Switching projects from the Load Workflow modal while a workflow is open no longer shows a
`GetWorkflowMetadata Failed` or `Failed to open` error for the previous project's workflow.
The bundled version of the Griptape Nodes app has been updated to `0.102.0`, with engine `0.105.0` and editor `0.129.0`.
When the engine fails to start because its bundled Python packages were changed outside the app (for example by `pip install`), the engine log now lists the changed packages and how to restore them.
The editor no longer shows a second engine picker next to the app's own engine controls.
**Try again** on "Can't reach your engine" now reconnects when the first connection timed out while the engine was still loading, instead of doing nothing until the app restarted.

The agent chat on Windows no longer fails on every message with "`LocalWorkspaceBackend` only
supports POSIX platforms" when the workspace has an `.agents/skills` folder. If a platform
cannot load skills, the chat now answers without them instead of failing.

Griptape Nodes Engine is pinned to 0.104.2. See its
[release notes](https://github.com/griptape-ai/griptape-nodes-engine/releases/tag/v0.104.2).
The bundled version of the Griptape Nodes app has been updated to `0.101.3`, with engine `0.104.2` and editor `0.128.1`.
Python modules in folders on `PYTHONPATH` when the app launches can now be imported from nodes. They are searched after the app's own packages, so they can't break the engine.
On Windows, the agent chat no longer fails on every message when the workspace has an `.agents/skills` folder.
In dark mode, the Direct and Cloud options in the Engine menu are readable.

Unlocking a node that was locked before it ever ran now lets the next downstream run execute it.
A run passing through a locked node marks it resolved without running it, and that state used
to outlive the unlock, so the node was skipped until it was run directly.
[#5766](https://github.com/griptape-ai/griptape-nodes-engine/issues/5766)

The editor no longer shows a "GetConfigValue Failed" popup for `library.sandbox_enabled` at
launch or on refresh. `GetConfigValueRequest` now succeeds with an empty value for a setting
that is unset by default, and fails only for a key that names no setting.

Griptape Nodes Engine is pinned to 0.104.1. See its
[release notes](https://github.com/griptape-ai/griptape-nodes-engine/releases/tag/v0.104.1).
The editor installed with the `editor` extra is pinned to 0.128.1.

With `websocket_direct` as the transport, such as the desktop app's direct mode, a node that
runs in a library's worker process now shows its progress bar, logs, and previews in the editor
while it runs, instead of only its final values once it finishes.

A node that runs in a library's worker process no longer flickers in the editor while it runs.
The worker no longer sends the editor changes to its own copy of the node, which made the editor
reload the node and drop the values shown so far.
The editor installed with the `editor` extra is pinned to 0.128.0.

In light mode, the "Cancel" and primary buttons in the Admin create and edit dialogs for license
keys and access groups are now readable instead of near-white on the light dialog background.

A hidden image or video parameter (`hide_property`) no longer leaves about 200px of empty space
in a newly placed node.

Each beta feature has thumbs up and thumbs down buttons, in the Beta Features popover in the
header and on Settings → "Beta Features", so you can tell us whether you like it. Your vote stays
selected. Click the other thumb to change it, or the same thumb to take it back. You can rate a
feature whether or not it's on. In the popover, the thumbs appear when you hover a feature's row.

A flask icon button in the header opens a beta features popover with a global on/off switch and a
toggle for each feature, grouped under Editor, Engine, and Libraries. The same switch and groups
appear in Settings → "Beta Features". Turning the global switch off disables every beta feature
at once and keeps your individual choices for when you turn it back on. The switch is saved to
your engine configuration as `beta_features.enabled`. The button shows a notification dot until
you open the popover for the first time.

The "Spend & Budgets and Usage Audit" admin beta feature adds two pages to the Admin Dashboard
sidebar: "Spend & Budgets", where organization admins set credit budgets for projects, license
keys and access groups, and "Usage Audit", which charts credit spend by project, license key,
access group and AI model. Turn it on from the flask button in the Admin Dashboard header. The
setting is saved in that browser only.
Deleting a secret in Settings → "API Keys & Secrets" asks for confirmation first.

A new or emptied canvas now shows the Griptape Nodes logo and "Press Tab to add your first node"
in the center. Clicking Tab in the hint opens the Add Node menu too, for when the mouse isn't over
